newsitem.title: USA: U.S. citizens urged to leave Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. citizens urged to leave Iraq.

text.p: The U.S. State Department on Monday urged all American citizens to leave Iraq, citing "soaring violence" in the north and Baghdad's "renewed campaign of repression."
The warning came amid reports that President Bill Clinton was on the verge of taking military action against Iraq in response to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's assault on Kurdish strongholds.

"The U.S. government views with grave concern the latest reports of soaring violence in northern Iraq. Given the government of Iraq's renewed campaign of repression, it is strongly recommended that all U.S. citizens leave Iraq," the State Department said.
The written statement said the U.S. government was contacting private organizations that had Americans in northern Iraq to urge that they be withdrawn immediately.
The United States said on Monday Iraqi troops appeared to be moving deeper into Kurdish opposition-held territory in northern Iraq, and Clinton had readied a "course of action" in response.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry refused to confirm that Clinton had signed off on military action, but he said that "clearly political, economic and military aspects have been under consideration."
